# Chrome counter values: int32 saturation and decimal-leading-zero (M3-T1 probe 7, for M3-01/M3-02)
# Source: tmp/m3probe/counters_gen.py -> counters.html (dev-only probe page, never committed to Go code), 2026-11-24, run by tmp/m3probe/run.sh: chromium --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --dump-dom,
# as Chromium 156.0.8078.73 built on Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) (headless, getBoundingClientRect). Units: integers as text.
# Format: {"name","reset" (counter-reset value on the container div, "" none),"increments" (counter-increment of each successive <p>),"out" per p: the text of counter(c) in "decimal" and "decimal-leading-zero"}. Each case is isolated in its own <section> (a counter-reset scopes to following siblings). Printed with --print-to-pdf and read with pdftotext -layout (pseudo-element text is not in the DOM).
# Findings: values saturate at int32 (2147483647 / -2147483648) for reset, increment and sums; an out-of-int32 integer is clamped; decimal-leading-zero pads 0..9 only: -5 prints "-5" (no padding for negatives), 7 "07", 0 "00", 123 "123".
# Invalid increments (1e3, 1.5, inherit) drop the whole declaration; the same name twice in counter-reset: the last wins; twice in counter-increment: both apply.
